proof.text: *Clause 1.* The inverse image $u^{-1}:\Ab(X_{\Et})\to\Ab(Y_{\Et})$ is an exact functor and carries short exact sequences to short exact sequences [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact]; applied to $0\to G_1\xrightarrow{\alpha}G\xrightarrow{\beta}G_2\to0$ it gives the exactness of $0\to u^{-1}G_1\xrightarrow{u^{-1}\alpha}u^{-1}G\xrightarrow{u^{-1}\beta}u^{-1}G_2\to0$ on $Y_{\Et}$.

*The two triangles.* Notation: for a scheme $T$ and an abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\Et}$ write $QF=F[0]$ for $F$ placed in degree $0$, an object of $\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ (its cohomology sheaves vanish outside degree $0$) [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Apply [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle] in the abelian category $\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] to $0\to G_1\to G\to G_2\to0$: $T_X=(QG_1\xrightarrow{Q\alpha}QG\xrightarrow{Q\beta}QG_2\xrightarrow{w_X}QG_1[1])$ is a distinguished triangle of $D(X_{\Et})$, $w_X$ the morphism constructed there. Its vertices lie in $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$, a strictly full triangulated subcategory of $D(X_{\Et})$ whose distinguished triangles are those of $D(X_{\Et})$ with vertices in it [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], so $T_X$ is distinguished in $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$. Likewise, by clause 1 (step 1), [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle] in $\Ab(Y_{\Et})$ gives the distinguished triangle $T_Y=(Q(u^{-1}G_1)\to Q(u^{-1}G)\to Q(u^{-1}G_2)\xrightarrow{w_Y}Q(u^{-1}G_1)[1])$ of $\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$, with maps $Q(u^{-1}\alpha)$, $Q(u^{-1}\beta)$.

proof.text: *$\RGamma$ of the triangles; the long exact sequences for $q\in\mathbf Z$.* For $T\in\{X,Y\}$ the global sections functor $\Gamma(T,-):\Ab(T_{\Et})\to\Ab$ (evaluation at the final object $T$) is additive and left exact (sums and kernels of abelian sheaves are computed sectionwise), and $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ has enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] (case $R=\mathbf Z$). So [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated] applies with $v=\Gamma(T,-)$: $\RGamma(T_{\Et},-)=R\Gamma(T,-):\Dplus(T_{\Et})\to\Dplus(\Ab)$, $\RGamma(T_{\Et},K)=\Gamma(T,I(K))$ for the chosen K-injective resolution $K\to I(K)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], and on morphisms through the homotopy class of the induced map of resolutions, is triangulated with the shift isomorphism $\sigma^T_K:\RGamma(T_{\Et},K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}\RGamma(T_{\Et},K)[1]$ (comparison of the resolutions $K[1]\to I(K[1])$ and $K[1]\to I(K)[1]$). Hence $\RGamma(T_{\Et},T_T)=(\RGamma(QF_1)\to\RGamma(QF)\to\RGamma(QF_2)\xrightarrow{\sigma^T_{QF_1}\circ\RGamma(w_T)}\RGamma(QF_1)[1])$, where $(F_1,F,F_2)=(G_1,G,G_2)$ for $T=X$ and $(u^{-1}G_1,u^{-1}G,u^{-1}G_2)$ for $T=Y$, is a distinguished triangle of $\Dplus(\Ab)$, hence of $D(\Ab)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. By [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] (in $D(\Ab)$, with $\mathcal H^q$ the cohomology of a representing complex) the sequence $\cdots\to\mathcal H^q\RGamma(QF_1)\to\mathcal H^q\RGamma(QF)\to\mathcal H^q\RGamma(QF_2)\xrightarrow{\delta^q_T}\mathcal H^{q+1}\RGamma(QF_1)\to\cdots$ is exact for all $q\in\mathbf Z$, its connecting map being $\mathcal H^q$ of the third morphism $\sigma^T_{QF_1}\circ\RGamma(T_{\Et},w_T)$ followed by the identification $\mathcal H^q(M[1])=\mathcal H^{q+1}(M)$ ($(M[1])^q=M^{q+1}$, the differential only changes sign) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; this is the $\delta^q_T$ of the statement.

proof.text: *Identification of the terms.* For $q\ge0$ and a sheaf $F$ on $T_{\Et}$, $\mathcal H^q(\RGamma(T_{\Et},QF))=\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(T,I(QF)))=H^q(T_{\Et},F)$ by [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] ($F\to I(QF)$ is a K-injective resolution of $F$). For a sheaf map $\varphi:F\to F'$, $\RGamma(T_{\Et},Q\varphi)$ is the class of $\Gamma(T,\tilde\varphi)$ for a map of the resolutions $\tilde\varphi$ lifting $\varphi$ up to homotopy [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated], so $\mathcal H^q(\RGamma(T_{\Et},Q\varphi))=\mathcal H^q(\Gamma(T,\tilde\varphi))=H^q(\varphi)$, the map of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (independent of $\tilde\varphi$ there). Hence in degrees $q\ge0$ the exact sequence of step 3 is $\cdots\to H^q(T,F_1)\xrightarrow{H^q(\alpha_T)}H^q(T,F)\xrightarrow{H^q(\beta_T)}H^q(T,F_2)\xrightarrow{\delta^q_T}H^{q+1}(T,F_1)\to\cdots$ with $(\alpha_X,\beta_X)=(\alpha,\beta)$ and $(\alpha_Y,\beta_Y)=(u^{-1}\alpha,u^{-1}\beta)$.

proof.text: *Start of the sequence (clause 2).* $\mathcal H^{-1}(\RGamma(T_{\Et},QF_2))=0$: the cohomology sheaves of $QF_2$ vanish in degrees $<0$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] (1) with $n=0$, in $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ (enough injectives, step 3) there are a complex $L$ of injective sheaves with $L^i=0$ for $i<0$ and an isomorphism $QL\cong QF_2$; by (2) of that node $L$ is K-injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit] (last sentence of its statement: a complex $\Gamma(T,I)$ computed from any K-injective $I$ with $QI\cong K$ is identified with $\RGamma(T_{\Et},K)$ by the canonical isomorphism) $\RGamma(T_{\Et},QF_2)\cong Q\Gamma(T,L)$, and $\Gamma(T,L)^{-1}=L^{-1}(T)=0$, so $\mathcal H^{-1}=0$. By exactness of step 3 at $\mathcal H^0\RGamma(QF_1)$, $\ker H^0(\alpha_T)=\operatorname{im}(\mathcal H^{-1}\RGamma(QF_2)\to H^0(T,F_1))=0$. With step 4 the sequence $0\to H^0(T,F_1)\to H^0(T,F)\to H^0(T,F_2)\xrightarrow{\delta^0_T}H^1(T,F_1)\to\cdots$ of the statement is exact at every place, for $T=X$ and for $T=Y$. This is clause 2.

proof.text: *$u^{-1}$ carries $T_X$ to $T_Y$.* The inverse image $u^{-1}:\Dplus(X_{\Et})\to\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$ is the restriction of the triangulated functor $u^{-1}_D$ induced by the exact functor $u^{-1}$ on abelian sheaves [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], with shift isomorphism $\iota_K:u^{-1}(K[1])\to(u^{-1}K)[1]$ the identity of termwise shifted complexes and with the natural isomorphism $\varphi_F:u^{-1}(QF)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(u^{-1}F)$ for sheaves in degree $0$ ($\varphi_{K^\bullet}$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] for $K^\bullet=F[0]$). By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-ses-triangle-image] for $F=u^{-1}$ and the sequence $0\to G_1\to G\to G_2\to0$, whose image sequence is the one of clause 1 with connecting morphism $w_Y$: $\varphi_{G_1}[1]\circ\iota_{QG_1}\circ u^{-1}(w_X)=w_Y\circ\varphi_{G_2}$, and $(\varphi_{G_1},\varphi_G,\varphi_{G_2})$ is an isomorphism of triangles from $u^{-1}T_X:=(u^{-1}QG_1,u^{-1}QG,u^{-1}QG_2,u^{-1}Q\alpha,u^{-1}Q\beta,\iota_{QG_1}\circ u^{-1}w_X)$ to $T_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift].

proof.text: *Naturality of $u^*$ on $\Dplus$.* For $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$, $u^*_K:\RGamma(X_{\Et},K)\to\RGamma(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}K)$ of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] equals $\lambda_{u^{-1}K}\circ\RGamma(X,\eta^D_{u,K})$ [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit] (2), with $\eta^D_u:\mathrm{id}\to Ru_*u^{-1}$ the unit of the adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction], a natural transformation, and $\lambda_L:\RGamma(X_{\Et},Ru_*L)\xrightarrow{\sim}\RGamma(Y_{\Et},L)$ natural in $L\in\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$ (clause 1 of the same node). For a morphism $a:K\to K'$ of $\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ (not necessarily induced by a map of complexes): $u^*_{K'}\circ\RGamma(X,a)=\lambda_{u^{-1}K'}\circ\RGamma(X,\eta^D_{K'}\circ a)=\lambda_{u^{-1}K'}\circ\RGamma(X,Ru_*u^{-1}a)\circ\RGamma(X,\eta^D_K)=\RGamma(Y,u^{-1}a)\circ\lambda_{u^{-1}K}\circ\RGamma(X,\eta^D_K)=\RGamma(Y,u^{-1}a)\circ u^*_K$ (functoriality of $\RGamma(X,-)$, naturality of $\eta^D$, naturality of $\lambda$ at $u^{-1}a$). So $u^*$ is a natural transformation $\RGamma(X_{\Et},-)\to\RGamma(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}(-))$ of functors $\Dplus(X_{\Et})\to\Dplus(\Ab)$.

proof.text: *$u^*$ commutes with the shift.* Claim: $\psi_K\circ u^*_{K[1]}=u^*_K[1]\circ\sigma^X_K$ for $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$, where $\psi_K:=\sigma^Y_{u^{-1}K}\circ\RGamma(Y,\iota_K):\RGamma(Y,u^{-1}(K[1]))\xrightarrow{\sim}\RGamma(Y,u^{-1}K)[1]$. Represent $K$ by a bounded below complex $K^\bullet$, choose a K-injective resolution $s:K^\bullet\to I$ and a K-injective resolution $r:u^{-1}I\to J$ on $Y_{\Et}$; then $u^*_K$ is the class of the map of complexes $c:\Gamma(X,I)\to\Gamma(Y,J)$, $c(a)=r(\eta_u(a))$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift], $s[1]:K^\bullet[1]\to I[1]$ is a K-injective resolution of $K^\bullet[1]$, and $r[1]:u^{-1}(I[1])=(u^{-1}I)[1]\to J[1]$ is a K-injective resolution (termwise $u^{-1}$ commutes with the shift: $(u^{-1}(I[1]))^n=u^{-1}I^{n+1}$ and $u^{-1}(-d)=-u^{-1}d$ by additivity). The recipe of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] for $K[1]$ with these resolutions gives the map $\Gamma(X,I[1])\to\Gamma(Y,J[1])$ which in degree $n$ is $c^{n+1}$, i.e. $c[1]$ (as complexes $\Gamma(T,M[1])=\Gamma(T,M)[1]$ termwise, since $\Gamma$ is additive). By [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (1) (independence of the resolutions for $K\in\Dplus$, up to the canonical isomorphisms between complexes computed from different resolutions) $u^*_{K[1]}$, computed from the chosen resolutions $K[1]\to I(K[1])$ and $u^{-1}(K[1])\to I(u^{-1}(K[1]))$, equals $c[1]$ after these canonical isomorphisms. On $X$ the canonical isomorphism $\RGamma(X,K[1])=\Gamma(X,I(K[1]))\cong\Gamma(X,I[1])=\Gamma(X,I)[1]\cong\RGamma(X,K)[1]$ is the comparison of the resolutions $K[1]\to I(K[1])$ and $K[1]\to I(K)[1]$ (comparisons of K-injective resolutions are unique up to homotopy and compose), which is $\sigma^X_K$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]; on $Y$ the canonical isomorphism $\RGamma(Y,u^{-1}(K[1]))\cong\Gamma(Y,J[1])=\Gamma(Y,J)[1]\cong\RGamma(Y,u^{-1}K)[1]$ is, for the same reason, $\sigma^Y_{u^{-1}K}\circ\RGamma(Y,\iota_K)=\psi_K$ ($\iota_K$ being the identity of the termwise shifted complexes [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]). This gives the claim. The analogous statement for $[n]$ follows by iteration but is not needed.

proof.text: *A morphism of triangles $\RGamma(X,T_X)\to\RGamma(Y,T_Y)$.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-triangle-morphism] with $\mathcal D=\Dplus(X_{\Et})$, $\mathcal D'=\Dplus(\Ab)$, $F_1=\RGamma(X_{\Et},-)$ with shift isomorphism $\sigma^X$, $F_2=\RGamma(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}(-))$ with $\psi$ of step 8, $\tau=u^*$ (natural by step 7, compatible with the shifts by step 8) and the triangle $T_X$: $(u^*_{QG_1},u^*_{QG},u^*_{QG_2})$ is a morphism of triangles from $\RGamma(X,T_X)$ (step 3) to $F_2T_X=(\RGamma(Y,u^{-1}QG_1),\RGamma(Y,u^{-1}QG),\RGamma(Y,u^{-1}QG_2),\ldots,\sigma^Y_{u^{-1}QG_1}\circ\RGamma(Y,\iota_{QG_1}\circ u^{-1}w_X))$. Next apply $\RGamma(Y,-)$ to the isomorphism of triangles $(\varphi_{G_1},\varphi_G,\varphi_{G_2}):u^{-1}T_X\to T_Y$ of step 6: the first two squares commute by functoriality of $\RGamma(Y,-)$, and the third because $\sigma^Y_{Q(u^{-1}G_1)}\circ\RGamma(Y,w_Y)\circ\RGamma(Y,\varphi_{G_2})=\sigma^Y_{Q(u^{-1}G_1)}\circ\RGamma(Y,\varphi_{G_1}[1])\circ\RGamma(Y,\iota_{QG_1}\circ u^{-1}w_X)=\RGamma(Y,\varphi_{G_1})[1]\circ\sigma^Y_{u^{-1}QG_1}\circ\RGamma(Y,\iota_{QG_1}\circ u^{-1}w_X)$ (step 6, then naturality of $\sigma^Y$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]). Composing [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift], $\theta=(\theta_{G_1},\theta_G,\theta_{G_2})$ with $\theta_F:=\RGamma(Y,\varphi_F)\circ u^*_{QF}:\RGamma(X,QF)\to\RGamma(Y,Q(u^{-1}F))$ is a morphism of triangles $\RGamma(X,T_X)\to\RGamma(Y,T_Y)$, both distinguished by step 3.

proof.text: *$\mathcal H^q(\theta_F)$ is the pullback map.* By [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit] (2), for an abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ placed in degree $0$, $u^*:H^q(X_{\Et},F)\to H^q(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}F)$ of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] is $\mathcal H^q$ of $u^*_{QF}$, where $u^{-1}(QF)$ is represented by the termwise complex $(u^{-1}F)[0]$ through $\varphi_F$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]; that is, $\mathcal H^q(\theta_F)=\mathcal H^q(\RGamma(Y,\varphi_F)\circ u^*_{QF})$ is the map $u^*:H^q(X_{\Et},F)\to H^q(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}F)$ in the identifications of step 4, for every $q\ge0$ (the identifications of K-injective resolutions are those of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (1)).

*Clause 3.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder] in $D(\Ab)$ to the morphism of distinguished triangles $\theta:\RGamma(X,T_X)\to\RGamma(Y,T_Y)$ of step 9: for every $q$, $\mathcal H^q(\theta_G)\circ\mathcal H^q(\RGamma(X,Q\alpha))=\mathcal H^q(\RGamma(Y,Q(u^{-1}\alpha)))\circ\mathcal H^q(\theta_{G_1})$, $\mathcal H^q(\theta_{G_2})\circ\mathcal H^q(\RGamma(X,Q\beta))=\mathcal H^q(\RGamma(Y,Q(u^{-1}\beta)))\circ\mathcal H^q(\theta_G)$ and $\mathcal H^{q+1}(\theta_{G_1})\circ\delta^q_X=\delta^q_Y\circ\mathcal H^q(\theta_{G_2})$, the connecting maps of that node being the $\delta^q_T$ of step 3. By step 4 and step 10 these read $u^*\circ H^q(\alpha)=H^q(u^{-1}\alpha)\circ u^*$, $u^*\circ H^q(\beta)=H^q(u^{-1}\beta)\circ u^*$ (also given by [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] (3)) and $u^*\circ\delta^q_X=\delta^q_Y\circ u^*:H^q(X_{\Et},G_2)\to H^{q+1}(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}G_1)$ for every $q\ge0$. This is clause 3.

title: Pullback maps form a morphism of long exact cohomology sequences
statement:
Let $u:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $0\to G_1\xrightarrow{\alpha}G\xrightarrow{\beta}G_2\to0$ be a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Then:

1. $0\to u^{-1}G_1\xrightarrow{u^{-1}\alpha}u^{-1}G\xrightarrow{u^{-1}\beta}u^{-1}G_2\to0$ is a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves on $Y_{\Et}$, $u^{-1}$ being the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].
2. For $T=X$ with the first sequence, and for $T=Y$ with the second, there are homomorphisms $\delta^q_T:H^q(T_{\Et},-_2)\to H^{q+1}(T_{\Et},-_1)$ ($q\ge0$) between the cohomology groups of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] (the connecting maps: $\delta^q_T$ is $\mathcal H^q$ of $\sigma^T\circ\RGamma(T_{\Et},w_T):\RGamma(T_{\Et},-_2)\to\RGamma(T_{\Et},-_1)[1]$ followed by the identification $\mathcal H^q(M[1])=\mathcal H^{q+1}(M)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], where $-_1[0]\to-[0]\to-_2[0]\xrightarrow{w_T}-_1[0][1]$ is the distinguished triangle of [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle] with $w_T$ the morphism constructed there (from the mapping cone; Mathlib's `singleδ`), $\RGamma(T_{\Et},-)$ acts on morphisms of $\Dplus(T_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] as the derived functor of $\Gamma(T,-)$ and $\sigma^T$ is its shift isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]) such that, with $H^q(\varphi)$ the map induced by a sheaf map $\varphi$ [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial],
$$0\to H^0(G_1)\to H^0(G)\to H^0(G_2)\xrightarrow{\delta^0}H^1(G_1)\to\cdots\to H^q(G_1)\xrightarrow{H^q(\alpha)}H^q(G)\xrightarrow{H^q(\beta)}H^q(G_2)\xrightarrow{\delta^q}H^{q+1}(G_1)\to\cdots$$
is exact on $X$, and likewise on $Y$ for the pulled-back sequence.
3. The pullback maps $u^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] form a morphism between these two long exact sequences: $u^*\circ H^q(\alpha)=H^q(u^{-1}\alpha)\circ u^*$, $u^*\circ H^q(\beta)=H^q(u^{-1}\beta)\circ u^*$, and $u^*\circ\delta^q_X=\delta^q_Y\circ u^*:H^q(X_{\Et},G_2)\to H^{q+1}(Y_{\Et},u^{-1}G_1)$ for every $q\ge0$.
